slides.title: New to speed skating and lost in jargon?
slides.sub: The words that matter and what to buy first

slides.title: Your platform is boot plus frame
slides.body: The boot holds your foot and ankle. The frame is the stiff beam that keeps your wheels in a straight line, so your push goes into the road.

slides.title: Start on 90mm to 100mm wheels
slides.body: Bigger wheels roll faster and carry speed. Smaller wheels feel more stable and quicker to get moving, which suits most beginners.

slides.title: Durometer is wheel hardness
slides.body: A higher number means a harder wheel. XFirm is softer with more grip. XXFirm is harder and rolls faster on smooth surfaces.

slides.title: Match the bore before you buy
slides.body: Inline speed bearings are 608s with an 8mm bore. Many quad skates use a 627 with a 7mm bore that does not fit an inline axle.

slides.title: Where the spacer sits
slides.caption: The spacer between the bearings lets you tighten the axle without pinching them.

slides.text: Neglect is what kills bearings, not age.
